cases.prompt: Our security alerts are so noisy the team closes them without reading. How do we fix the detections?
assertions: Measures precision per rule and routes by precision band rather than paging on everything
Tunes with identity and behavioural context instead of raising count thresholds, which hides slow attackers
Retires or fixes rules with no fires and documents false positives inside the rule

cases.prompt: Which detections should we write first, and how do we know our MITRE ATT&CK coverage is real?
assertions: Maps required telemetry per attacker behaviour before writing rules, naming the common collection gaps
Scores each technique none / logged-only / detected / detected-and-tested rather than claiming a heat map
Validates with Atomic Red Team execution and measures detection latency as the floor on dwell time

cases.prompt: Write our detection content as code in Sigma with tests in CI, and set up a hunt for a stolen CI token.
assertions: Stores vendor-neutral Sigma rules in Git and compiles them per backend, failing CI on schema drift
Gives every tuning filter an owner, a reason and a review date
Frames the hunt as a time-boxed hypothesis whose deliverable is a saved query or a new detection

cases.prompt: A leaked AWS access key was already used by an attacker — contain it and preserve evidence.
Instrument our services with OpenTelemetry so a latency spike leads to the exact trace.
